falsification_tests: a seeded broken plugin module (import error in a fixture copy of the registry build) under which the suite still passes; or a registered count by category in the running system that differs from the pinned count while CI is green.
claims.text: Registry completeness is pinned, and a silent shrink fails CI.** A CI registry-completeness test pins the plugin module list (all 144 experiment_graph_*.py modules) and the registered node count by category; outside production leniency, a plugin module that fails to import fails the test loudly instead of shrinking the registry behind a log warning. This does not establish: that the pinned counts are the right counts - only that any change to them is a visible, recorded act rather than an accident.

falsification_tests: two importable definitions of one id in the tree; a fixture registering an already-registered id that the suite accepts; or fixture outputs showing the deleted definition's behaviour where the kept definition's was recorded as correct.
claims.text: No node id has two live definitions.** Exactly one definition of each node id is reachable in the built registry; the three shadowed classes of census Table 4 (IndusPhase254SemanticConstraint, IndusPhase255CommodityPhonemes, IndusPhase256LEExtension) are resolved to the behaviour-verified definition, the dead definition is deleted, and a duplicate-id registration in a test fixture fails the suite. This does not establish: that the kept definition computes the right science - only that there is one of it, chosen by a recorded behaviour diff, where before there were two and the choice was an import order.

falsification_tests: a component test (or manual run) with the catalog endpoint failing in which the builder shows an empty palette with no error surface.
claims.text: A failed palette load is visible, never a silent empty.** When the Experiment Builder's catalog fetch fails, the builder renders an error state that names the failure; it never renders an empty palette indistinguishable from 'no nodes exist'. This does not establish: that the catalog endpoint is reliable - only that its failure can no longer masquerade as an empty registry.

falsification_tests: a node in the default catalog response that is flagged legacy; a non-legacy registered node missing from it; or a palette-only id that exists in no registry.
claims.text: The palette is the registry minus legacy, mechanically.** The catalog endpoint's default response contains exactly the registered nodes not flagged legacy: GENERIC nodes, parameterized PARTIAL nodes, and the live working set. The palette set is computed from the registry and the flag, never maintained as a separate list. This does not establish: that the legacy classification of any individual node is correct - the classification of record is the census's, and reclassifying a node is a recorded stage act, not a consequence of this claim.

falsification_tests: a stored graph, ledger metadata entry, or test fixture referencing a wrapper id that resolved before S2 and fails to resolve after it.
claims.text: Legacy nodes stay resolvable; nothing stored dangles.** Every node id resolvable before Stage S2 remains resolvable after it, through the same ATOMIC_NODES table; the full registry (including legacy) is what graph loading, the metadata merge, and resolution consult. This does not establish: that legacy nodes produce current or correct results - only that history stays loadable. The _archive/ graphs are outside this claim (spec non-goals).

falsification_tests: a PARTIAL node with no disposition, with two, or whose disposition record lacks the evidence its class requires (for (c), any of the bar's three legs).
claims.text: Every PARTIAL domain node is triaged exactly once, on evidence.** Each of the 68 PARTIAL domain nodes of the census carries exactly one Stage S3 disposition - (a) converted to a generic primitive, (b) re-expressed as a composition of primitives in its consuming experiments, or (c) retained under the D3 bar - recorded in the triage record with its evidence; the domain-flavoured ids in live use are triaged first. This does not establish: that the dispositions are the best possible - only that each one exists, is singular, and is backed by the evidence its class demands.

falsification_tests: a converted node whose source still branches on a domain identity; or two parameter settings of a converted node that cannot reproduce the behaviours of the domain variants it replaced, on their pinned fixtures.
claims.text: A converted node carries its domain content in parameters, not in code.** For every node converted under disposition (a), the domain specifics (corpus, language, code table, weights) arrive as parameter or port data; the node's code contains no branch on a domain identity (a named language, corpus, scholar map, or sign list). This does not establish: that the primitive is elegant or complete - only that the domain content moved from code to data, which is the coupling property the owner directed.

falsification_tests: a node in the manual reference that is not in the palette set; a palette node missing from it; a port or param in the manual that differs from the registry's; or a hand edit inside a generated block that CI accepts.
claims.text: The manual's node reference is the palette set, mechanically.** The generated node reference (user-manual block and the HelpView data module) lists exactly the palette set of claim C087-4, with each node's category, ports, and params as the registry states them; the CI conformance test of Stage S4 regenerates and diffs, failing on drift in either direction. This does not establish: that the surrounding prose is clear or complete - the claim covers the enumerable reference, the part that was mechanically false.

falsification_tests: any of the 10 phantom names appearing in a manual surface while CI is green; or a generated experiment list whose count differs from the graph files on disk.
claims.text: No manual names a node or experiment that does not exist.** No manual surface (user-manual, USER_GUIDE, HelpView) names any of the 10 phantom node names of census Table 3, enforced by absence checks in the same CI conformance test; and USER_GUIDE's active-experiments list is generated from the graph files on disk (27 today), neither more nor fewer. This does not establish: that the manuals are well written - only that their enumerable claims about what exists are true.

falsification_tests: a shipped Logs surface missing a tab, a control, or a field the approved wireframes carry; a records tab that can mutate a record; or a Playwright comparison against the approved screens that fails while the stage is reported done.
claims.text: The Logs view is restored, to the approved wireframes.** The app carries a Logs surface with the two tabs of the owner-approved S5 wireframes package: a live stream tab consuming GET /terminal/log and GET /terminal/log/stream, and a records tab reading the jobs/job_results, phase_actions, and notification_log tables, read-only, with per-record detail expansion. The build matches the approved wireframes screen by screen under Playwright verification. This does not establish: that the terminal endpoints scale or that the SSE tail survives the cloud edge - the claim covers the desktop surface the wireframes draw.

falsification_tests: documentation surfaces disagreeing about the bus's semantics; behaviour contradicting the statement (for the documented-ephemeral ruling: any surface promising delivery or replay; for a persistence ruling: an event emitted with no subscriber that is not later retrievable); or the pinning test removed while the statement remains.
claims.text: The events bus's persistence semantics are stated once, and the code matches the statement.** Exactly one documented statement (module docstring, user manual, and HelpView, in agreement) declares whether events are persisted or ephemeral-by-design and what a subscriber can rely on; the emit path's behaviour matches the statement, and the statement's presence is pinned by a test. This does not establish: that the ruled disposition is the ideal one - only that it is a decision, stated where a reader looks, and true of the code.

falsification_tests: a deleted set whose (name, language, pairs content) differs from its group's kept set in any element; a distinct content with no surviving copy; a deletion performed by direct database write; or a removed id absent from the stage record.
claims.text: Anchor-set dedupe removes exact duplicates only, through the API, on the record.** Stage S6 deletes an anchor set only when another set with identical (name, language, pairs content) is kept; the earliest canonical copy of each distinct content survives; every deletion goes through DELETE /anchor-sets/{id}; and every removed id, with its group's kept id, is recorded in the stage record. This does not establish: that the surviving sets are good data - placeholder content that is distinct survives this stage by design; judging it is a separate act.

claims.text: Every live graph still resolves and runs with byte-identical results.** After each of S2 and S3, all 27 live graphs resolve every atomicId they reference, and the pinned comparison runs produce results byte-identical to their pre-stage records. This does not establish: that the graphs' results are correct - only that this program did not change them, which is the non-goal the owner set.

claims.text: This program changes no verdict, claim status, or ledger content.** No stage of Spec 087 alters an Indus claim's status, stage, or score, appends or edits a ledger entry, or modifies a frozen record; the claims ledger and the freeze records are byte-identical before and after the program. This does not establish: anything about the truth of any claim - the program is about the tool, not the decipherment.

falsification_tests: a merged stage PR whose behaviour change has no corresponding manual change in the same PR, where the stage record does not name why no manual surface is affected.
claims.text: Manual updates land with the behaviour.** Every stage PR that changes user-visible behaviour updates the affected manual surfaces (user-manual, USER_GUIDE, HelpView as applicable) in the same PR; no stage merges with its manual update deferred to a later PR. This does not establish: that the updates are well written - only that they are not late, which is the failure F7 documents at scale.

falsification_tests: a module named node_registry.py in the tree after S1 without the recorded owner ruling for option (b); a broken /node-registry/ endpoint; or a document that still points a reader at the old name for the experiment registry.
claims.text: The Study Builder's schema module no longer impersonates the node registry.** After Stage S1, the module formerly named node_registry.py is renamed (study_node_registry.py) or, if the owner rules otherwise, carries a header and a docs entry stating it is the Study Builder's param-schema module; its endpoint (GET /node-registry/{node_type}/{ref_id}) answers unchanged, and both registries import in one process without ambiguity. This does not establish: that the two node systems should be merged - only that they stop sharing a name.

falsification_tests: a merged PR that alters the pinned counts without a stage record naming the alteration; or runtime counts differing from the pin while CI is green.
claims.text: The registry changes only by recorded acts.** After S2's re-pin, the registered count and the per-category census in the completeness test change only through a Spec 087 stage PR that names the change in its stage record; the count never moves as a side effect of an unrelated change. This does not establish: that the registry should never grow - new primitives are welcome; this claim makes their arrival an act, not an accident.
